decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach to left wrench and right pliers, gradually pitching both grippers downward; table height and fingertip offset need visual refinement.
Retry from unchanged home with much smaller initial increments to preserve IK continuity while entering the approach configuration.
Continue the overhead approach and finish downward orientation, maintaining lateral workspace separation and open grippers.
RGB suggests a higher tabletop than initially estimated. Raise clear, refine wrench and pliers alignment inward, and complete downward pitch with small increments.
Descend slowly over the wrench handle and pliers handles; maintain vertical grippers and refine right alignment slightly inward.
Close around both tool handles and perform a short vertical retention test; right-side contact may be with the nearby tape measure, so verify visually.
Wrench appears retained; carry it above the tray. Right grasp missed, so reopen and approach pliers nearer their pivot and lower before retrying.
Wrench slipped onto the tabletop; reapproach its new horizontal handle orientation. Close the right gripper at the pliers pivot and test retention vertically.
Move retained pliers cautiously above the right side of the tray for slot inspection; re-align the left gripper to the wrench's latest resting position.
Lower the right arm away from its high-reach IK boundary while orienting pliers over the tray. Regrasp the horizontal wrench and begin a gentle lift.
Pliers have settled onto the tray; open and withdraw the right gripper toward the tape measure. Lift the left gripper vertically to check the wrench grasp before transporting.
Left wrench was not retained: reopen, lower further, and correct transverse handle alignment using the wrist image. Approach tape measure with the right gripper.
Grasp the visually centered wrench handle at the lower height, and descend to grasp the tape measure. Use slow vertical tests to avoid dragging either tool.
Both objects now appear between the jaws. Lift clear, then carry the wrench toward the lower long recess and tape toward the right compact recess, with closed grippers.
Wrench remains held, so align over the tray's bottom horizontal recess and begin lowering. Tape fell back onto the table; reopen and reapproach its new center.
Seat and release the wrench into the lower long recess. Regrasp the tape measure more deeply at its body center rather than its upper edge.
Withdraw from the released wrench without disturbing it. Test tape retention with a straight lift before transporting, while the left arm starts toward the remaining hammer.
Wrench remains released in its lower recess. Approach the hammer with the left arm; tape slipped, so correct its grasp rearward to the actual body center and descend open.
Close on the recentered tape and test a vertical lift. Align the left gripper vertically and descend over the hammer's black handle.
Tape appears retained after the corrected lift; carry toward its compact right-hand recess. Center the hammer handle between left jaws, close, and lift gently.
Raise and rotate the retained hammer toward the top horizontal recess, keeping the left wrist left of center. Lower the tape measure over the compact right-side slot.
Replan from the interrupted pose with smaller hammer translation and downward motion to maintain IK continuity. Finish horizontal alignment; release tape into its compact recess and withdraw.
Correct the malformed row from the unchanged observation. Lower and move the hammer with small continuous increments; withdraw the open right gripper from the released tape.
Hammer head is still outside its recess. Release and regrasp closer to the head so it can be translated inward without the left wrist crossing center. Clear the right arm laterally.
Regrasp the hammer's exposed metal shaft closer to its head, using a small alignment correction and slow descent; keep the right arm clear.
The wide-open jaws contacted the tray rim. Lift, move to the inner shaft/handle junction, and narrow the aperture before descending to avoid the rim.
Correct the rejected tensor from the unchanged pose. Close, lift the hammer slightly, and start its small inward alignment while the right arm remains still.
The hammer did not follow the last lift. Reopen narrowly and descend farther onto the handle, then close without lateral movement to improve depth of engagement.
Test the deeper hammer grasp and translate it a short distance into the top recess, correcting its slight diagonal while keeping the left wrist on its own side.
Correct the rejected row from the unchanged pose. Release the hammer and clear the left arm, then approach its right-side handle with the right arm without crossing.
Avoid the left arm's high-pose IK boundary by moving outward and slightly downward from the latest pose. Bring the right arm toward the hammer handle at a lower approach height.
Retry the unchanged pose with submillimeter left-arm increments, gradually increasing only while moving away from the IK boundary. Continue a slow right-side approach.
Clear the left arm for an unobstructed slot view. Approach the hammer's right-side handle using the right arm and a narrowed aperture to avoid the tray walls.
Right wrist view shows the hammer behind the current grip line, near the pliers. Raise slightly and shift toward the hammer handle while clearing the left arm.
Replan from the IK interruption by lowering the right wrist away from its high-reach boundary before continuing toward the hammer, using small continuous increments.
Shift the right grasp slightly along the hammer handle rather than beyond its end, maintaining positive wrist x and a narrow aperture near the rear tray wall; close gently.

The right arm reached an IK boundary. Close at the current handle alignment, then move outward and slightly backward with small increments, which also tests retention and improves hammer placement if grasped.
Use submillimeter initial right-arm retreat increments to leave the near-singular pose, increasing gradually. Begin returning the clear left arm toward its initial position and orientation.
Wrist RGB suggests the hammer lies beyond the right grasp line. Use a small forward wrist tilt instead of extending the arm toward its IK limit, then close. Finish the left-arm reset.
Refine the right-hand hammer grasp slightly toward the handle interior and forward with a small tilt; avoid further arm extension. Settle the left arm at its initial pose.
Lift and translate the newly aligned hammer grasp slightly rightward to bring its head inside the top recess; keep the reset left arm stationary and verify retention.
RGB shows the right grasp retained the pliers, not the hammer. Return the pliers to their central recess, straighten the wrist, and release before further hammer adjustment.
Clear the right gripper from the released pliers. Try a horizontal left-side approach to the exposed hammer head, avoiding the crowded handle area and maintaining elbow-up continuity.
Retry the rejected departure from home with smaller initial left-arm increments, gradually increasing while retaining the current IK branch. Right arm withdraws from the tray.
The low horizontal path is continuity-limited. Switch to a raised, gradually downward-pitched approach to the exposed hammer head while keeping the elbow-up branch; continue clearing the right arm.
Approach the exposed hammer head from above with the left arm rather than the crowded handles. Keep the other tools undisturbed and continue right-arm retreat.
After the interrupted approach, use smaller increments to align over the exposed hammer head and close with a narrowed aperture. Continue returning the right arm toward origin.
The left jaws now surround the hammer head. Lift slightly and shift it inward over the top slot while completing the right-arm reset.
Hammer did not follow the last lift. Recenter the left jaws on the solid head farther forward and left, rather than the claw tips, then close at the observed head height.
Test the recentered hammer-head grasp with a small lift and short inward/backward translation toward the top recess; hold the right arm at origin.
The hammer again stayed behind; account for the pinch point's offset from link6 by pitching slightly forward and lowering onto the head, rather than aligning link6 directly above it.
Hammer has slid behind the tray. Use the wrist view to correct directly toward the head's new center and lower to tabletop grasp height, preserving the forward tilt.
The hammer head is now visibly between the jaws. Lift clear and carry it inward and slightly back over the top recess, maintaining the grasp orientation.
The head grasp slipped on lifting. Switch to the exposed metal shaft on the tabletop; approach upright and plan a deeper grasp away from the tray rim.
Rotate the jaws across the hammer shaft and lower to a deeper tabletop grasp, compensating for the offset between link6 and the pinch center.
Wrist view places the shaft just outside the right jaw. Tilt the pinch point toward it without extending the arm further, then close at the lower shaft height.
The shaft now appears engaged between the jaws. Lift vertically, then carry the hammer inward and back toward the top recess without changing the grasp orientation.
The shaft slipped free. Use wrist-image alignment to grasp the thicker black handle instead, moving forward and descending more deeply before closing.
The near jaw contacted the tray wall before closing. Lift clear, shift the grip farther behind the tray toward the handle center, narrow the jaws, and descend again.
After IK interruption, avoid further forward translation. Lower and add a small forward wrist tilt to reach the handle while moving away from the folded-arm boundary, then close.
The gripper is obstructed by the tray, with significant tracking error. Withdraw open and upward into the left workspace before attempting a clear approach to the hammer.
Reapproach the hammer handle from farther behind the tray with a forward-tilted wrist. Preshape the jaws above the tool so the near finger stays clear of the tray wall during descent.
Descend with the preshaped jaws behind the tray, keeping the approach fixed so the final handle alignment can be checked before closing.
At the lower height the handle is left of the pinch center in the wrist image. Make a small transverse correction and close without changing height.
The handle is centered, but pad engagement remains uncertain. Reopen narrowly and lower another small increment before closing to improve contact depth.
Perform only a slow vertical retention test after the deeper handle grasp; avoid lateral transport until the hammer visibly follows.
The hammer stayed on the table during the test. Lower the tilted gripper further to engage the sides of the handle, using a narrow aperture and small transverse correction.
Make a final small centering correction at the handle junction, close, and test retention with only a short vertical lift.
